signals.title: USD/JPY — Geopolitical Safe-Haven + Hawkish Fed Shift
signals.text: Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz creates an immediate safe-haven bid for JPY, though USD/JPY closed Friday at 160.04 following hawkish comments from Fed Chair Warsh. While JPY COT leveraged funds are net short -81,619 (pctl 9), the geopolitical escalation risks a sharp short-covering squeeze against the +266bp USD carry advantage. Fed holds at 3.75%. Trade bias: Bullish JPY (Bearish USD/JPY) on geopolitical escalation; hawkish Fed rhetoric caps the downside. Catalyst: Sydney open response to Strait of Hormuz closure. Risk: De-escalation headlines or focus shifting entirely to the US yield advantage above 4.72%.
evidence: IRGC Navy: Strait of Hormuz closed
Fed Chair Warsh: September hike odds 57%

signals.title: AUD/CHF — G10 Bilateral Theme + Risk-Off Divergence
signals.text: AUD outperformed all G10 peers this week (1W avg +1.301%) while CHF remained the laggard (-0.623%), creating a significant 1.924% bilateral spread. Despite the AUD strength, the weekend's geopolitical TIER-1 event favors the CHF safe-haven over the high-beta AUD, especially with AUD/CHF retail sentiment at an extreme 95% short. The +435bp carry advantage for AUD faces a major stress test as risk-off flows typically trigger rapid carry unwinds in CHF crosses. Trade bias: Bearish AUD/CHF into the open; safe-haven demand overrides the weekly momentum. Catalyst: Sydney open response to geopolitical risk. Risk: Markets ignore geopolitics and extend the G10 scorecard momentum trend.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Hawkish Divergence + Momentum Breakdown
signals.text: EUR COT leveraged funds shifted heavily net short (-55,311, pctl 3) after EUR/USD fell -0.86% this week to close at 1.1587. The pair is now trading below its SMA20 (1.1593) and SMA200 (1.1637), signaling a technical breakdown as the SOFR-ESTR carry spread (+145bp) favors the USD. Although the ECB has a hike bias for the September 10th meeting, the Fed's 57% hike probability for September maintains downward pressure on the pair. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD; momentum and yield spread favor the downside toward the SMA50 at 1.149. Catalyst: next ECB meeting (mkt: 75% hike priced). Risk: ESI outperformance (Index +13.1) triggers a relief rally if U.S. data misses.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Positioning Exhaustion + Carry Buffer
signals.text: GBP COT leveraged funds are net long +56,839 (pctl 96), indicating a crowded long position that is vulnerable to a reversal following Friday's -0.41% decline. The GBP/USD closed at 1.3537, sitting just below its SMA20 (1.354), as the Fed's hawkish pivot erodes the GBP carry advantage (SONIA 3.73% vs SOFR 3.64%). Elevated options hedging demand (VRP +6.0%) suggests traders are increasingly buying protection against further downside. Trade bias: Bearish GBP/USD on positioning unwind; high IV (11.0%) vs HV30 (5.0%) confirms bearish anxiety. Catalyst: next BoE meeting (mkt: 100% hold priced). Risk: UK 10Y yield premium (+43bp vs US) widens further, attracting defensive flows.
